sourceFacts.fact: In pseudostrabismus the eyes are aligned despite an apparent crossed appearance, often related to facial features.
Symmetric positions of corneal light reflections support alignment, while asymmetric positions prompt assessment for true misalignment.

layoutSpecification: Title 'Compare reflection positions'. Draw an abstract comparison of positional symmetry, NOT patient eyes or simulated diagnostic media. LEFT panel heading 'Matched positions': two identical large flat teal discs side by side, EACH with a tiny ivory dot exactly at its centre. Each disc has a very faint horizontal and vertical centre guide. Below 'Supports alignment'. RIGHT panel heading 'Different positions': two identical discs; the LEFT disc has an ivory dot exactly centred, the RIGHT disc has an ivory dot clearly shifted to the RIGHT of its centre guide. Below 'Assess for misalignment'. Use plain circles without eyelids, iris texture, pupils, lashes, sclera or face. Bottom 'Abstract reflection-position model'. Do not label these dots as a definitive diagnosis. Two discs in each group, four total.
